Owners: V2-034 owns the manifest fields (landed) and V2-074 owns the compatibility decision (what may read a reported contract release or Runner API range). (4) bundle -- bundle_digest, candidate_id: NOT reported; same measurement and the same two owners. internal/release/bundle.go:293 and :449 produce a release-candidate ContractDigest, which is a different claim about a source tree, not a module manifest field. (5) provenance -- key_id, algorithm: NOT reported; same measurement and the same two owners. Sixth row, as required: this task introduces NO canonical schema counter and NO advance operation. currentSchema exists only as a parameter -- of update.Verify at internal/update/update.go:127, update.Install at :220 and update.VerifyInstalled at :296 (the Work Order's :41 and :71 are stale line numbers for the same two-then-three functions). checks.name: A4-validation-is-shape-only-and-a-partial-object-stores-nothing
checks.summary: Four tests PASS. Version shape: 6 accepted literals (0.1.0, 1.2.3, 10.20.30, 0.1.0-dev, 1.0.0-rc.1, 2.0.0-alpha-3) and 9 rejected (empty string, 1.2 bare major.minor, v1.2.3 leading v, 1.2.3-RC1 uppercase prerelease, 1.2.3.4, 1.2.3- trailing hyphen, leading space, trailing space, 01.2.3-A). Digest shape: 4 accepted (two 64-hex literals plus 64 zeroes and 64 f) and 6 rejected (empty, 63 chars, 65 chars, uppercase, non-hex g*64, sha256: prefix). Interval shape: 3 accepted ([1,1], [1,4096], [4096,4096]) and 5 rejected (schema_min 0, schema_min -1, schema_max below schema_min, schema_max above the 4096 ceiling, schema_min above the ceiling), each refusal errors.Is ErrRunnerVersionReportInvalid. PARTIAL-OBJECT VERDICT: TestPartialRunnerVersionObjectIsRefusedAndStoresNothing refuses 9 strict subsets of the four-field object -- schema_max alone, schema_min alone, version alone, digest alone, interval without binary, binary without interval, everything but schema_min, everything but the digest, and the wholly empty object -- and for each one asserts (a) the call errors with ErrRunnerVersionReportInvalid, (b) the keyed read of the report finds nothing, (c) the bounded enumeration returns zero rows, and (d) zero events and zero outbox items were recorded. schema_max without schema_min is refused rather than stored as an interval starting at zero. TestHeartbeatWithoutAReportStoresNothingAndErasesNothing asserts the other half: a heartbeat that omits runner_version returns success and stores no report at all, the Runner still enumerates with report_state not-reported, and after a real report a later report-less heartbeat leaves the stored record byte-identical (struct equality) rather than zeroing it -- which is the failure dp-v2-069 d3 rejected domain.RunnerObservation for.

checks.name: A5-the-runner-clock-cannot-enter-the-record
checks.summary: TestReportedAtIsTheTransactionAuthorityTime PASS. The request object has no timestamp field at all -- asserted as part of the A3 scan, where RunnerVersionInput is exactly [Version BinarySHA256 SchemaMin SchemaMax]. The stored reported_at is compared with the At of the event the same heartbeat recorded, not with a fresh clock read: time.Time.Equal plus an RFC3339Nano string comparison, so the two are byte-identical in the wire encoding as well. The clock injected for this test advances one second per call, so a value taken from any other read of the clock would differ; the test also asserts the clock was consulted at least twice, so the advancing control is in force rather than a frozen instant making the equality incidental. reported_at is derived by transactionAuthorityTime, which is the same derivation Service.record uses: the unit of work's AuthorityContext plus the authorityTimeKey value that Service.mutate captured once before the transaction callback.

checks.name: A5-reported-at-is-stable-across-a-transaction-retry
checks.summary: TestReportedAtIsStableAcrossATransactionRetry PASS, driven deterministically at the application boundary. A replayTransactor re-invokes the transaction callback three times the way Firestore re-invokes it after an aborted attempt -- the first two attempts' staged writes are discarded and the callback runs again on a fresh unit of work with the same context -- with no goroutine, no contention and no sleep. Assertions: the injected advancing clock is consulted exactly twice for one Heartbeat regardless of the attempt count (one read for the request's own instant, one for the transaction's), so no attempt re-read the clock; exactly one event survives, so the discarded attempts leaked nothing; and the surviving report's reported_at equals the surviving event's At.

checks.name: A5-firestore-contention-retry-path
checks.summary: SKIPPED, and not counted as a pass (gate rule G7). Reason: cloud.google.com/go/firestore retries a transaction callback only on an ABORTED status, which requires a genuinely concurrent conflicting writer. Forcing that needs a goroutine or a timed race, and the Work Order's determinism constraint (A15) forbids both -- no goroutine, no wall-clock timer, no fixed sleep in any new test. The property the Firestore retry path would demonstrate is asserted deterministically instead by the check above: the authority instant is captured once, in Service.mutate, before s.tx.Transact is called, so the number of times the adapter re-invokes the callback cannot change it. What was actually executed against the emulator is recorded in the store-firestore checks of this task's api record and in the summaries above; no claim is made here about real Firestore contention behaviour.

checks.name: A6-three-states-no-default-interval-explicit-unknown
checks.summary: Five tests PASS, all with an injected clock and no sleep. (a) A Runner with no report reports report_state not-reported and the marshalled JSON carries none of version, binary_sha256, schema_min, schema_max or reported_at -- absence of the keys is asserted on the document, so no interval of [0,0] or any other synthesized value can appear. (b) One valid report reports report_state reported with all four coordinates echoed exactly (1.2.3, the 64-hex digest, 2, 7). (c) Moving the injected clock past the declared staleness window turns the same row into report_state stale with every coordinate byte-identical to the reported row, so nothing is silently refreshed or dropped; the boundary instant itself is still reported, one nanosecond past it is stale. (d) intersection_state is unknown whenever any enumerated Runner is not in state reported: with no Runner known at all, with exactly one of two Runners reporting, and with one Runner whose report has gone stale. (e) Two Runners reporting [2,7] and [4,9] give non-empty with endpoints 4 and 7 -- the maximum of the minima and the minimum of the maxima. (f) Two Runners reporting [1,3] and [5,9] give empty, and the marshalled document then carries no endpoint keys at all. (g) TestRunnerEnumsAreClosed parses runner_version.go with go/ast and requires, for RunnerReportState and SchemaIntersectionState both, that the set of constants declared with that type equals the set of identifiers appearing as case values in that type's Valid() switch -- so a constant added without a case fails, and a case added without a constant fails. The matcher is verified first against a synthetic type whose switch is deliberately missing one case, and a scan that found nothing is a Fatal. The runtime side is asserted too: every declared value is Valid and none of "", compatible, ok, healthy, valid is. (h) TestRunnerViewNeverSpellsCompatibleWithoutUnknown walks the marshalled JSON of four different views recursively, collecting 13 distinct keys and 11 distinct string values, and asserts that no key and no value contains compatible, ok, healthy or valid, and that unknown, not-reported and stale all actually appear -- so unknown is a reachable sibling value rather than a constant nothing emits.

checks.name: A9-both-store-adapters-one-behavioural-table
checks.summary: TestRunnerVersionReportBehaviouralTable PASS: the memory adapter satisfied 5 shared cases. The table is application.RunnerVersionReportCases(), exported data in internal/application that imports nothing and asserts nothing, so internal/store/memory and internal/store/firestore run the SAME cases by value and only the driver is local; the memory store therefore cannot pass behaviour the Firestore store does not implement. Cases: one report round-trips through a read in a separate transaction; the last writer wins per RunnerID and leaves exactly one row; a Runner known only through a report-less heartbeat enumerates with a zero ReportedAt and zero coordinates; the order is RunnerID ascending rather than insertion order; more reports than the bound are truncated and the truncation is reported. Every reported row is also read back by key in its own transaction. TestRunnerVersionReportRollbackLeaksNothing PASS: a rolled-back transaction commits no report -- neither the keyed read nor the enumeration sees it -- and a report with an empty runner id is refused rather than stored under the empty key. No existing operation's quota reservation shape was changed: quota.ReadTransactionUsage and quota.MutationUsage are untouched and no ReserveQuota call site was modified.

checks.name: A12-shapes-are-pinned-without-an-import
checks.summary: TestApplicationImportsNeitherUpdateNorScheduler PASS: a go/ast import scan over all 17 .go files of internal/application, test files included, covering 134 import paths, asserts that none is internal/update or internal/scheduler or a subpackage of either. A zero-path scan is a Fatal. The semver shape at internal/application/runner_version.go and the 64-hex digest shape beside it are literal copies by value of internal/update/update.go:64 and :65. Recorded plainly, as dp-v2-069 d12 requires: the two declarations CAN drift, no compiler or test in internal/update will notice, and the only thing that will catch it is TestRunnerVersionShapesArePinnedToTheUpdatePatterns, whose name says what it pins and which asserts the same verdict for 6 accepted and 9 rejected version literals and 4 accepted and 6 rejected digest literals.

checks.name: A11-idempotency-consequence-asserted-not-assumed
checks.summary: TestHeartbeatReplayWithAChangedReportIsAConflict PASS. Replaying one heartbeat request_id with an identical runner_version restores the prior response (reflect.DeepEqual on the response value). Replaying the same request_id with a different runner_version returns application.ErrIdempotencyConflict, and so does replaying it with the object dropped entirely. The conflict path stores nothing new: the stored report is byte-identical before and after (struct equality) and no new event was recorded. This follows from requestFingerprint("heartbeat", req) at internal/application/service.go, which hashes the whole request struct, and it is EXISTING semantics rather than new behaviour -- any changed field of a replayed heartbeat has always produced this conflict, and a heartbeat loop already needs a fresh request_id per heartbeat. The status code the transport maps it to is 409, recorded in this task's api evidence. One further consequence is recorded in docs/operations/runner-version-report.md section 3 rather than hidden: adding a field to the request struct changes the fingerprint of an otherwise identical request, so an idempotency record written by an older binary and replayed against a newer one is a conflict.

checks.name: A15-determinism-is-acceptance
checks.summary: Run three times in sequence; with the elapsed-time measurements normalised the output of all three runs is byte-identical (diff of run 1 vs 2 and run 2 vs 3 both empty), and the verdict lines are the same each time: 'ok github.com/takushi/agentic-loop-foundation/v2/internal/application' and 'ok github.com/takushi/agentic-loop-foundation/v2/internal/api'. Also run once with -race: both packages ok (1.239s and 1.117s). No new test contains a fixed sleep, a wall-clock timer or a goroutine: every instant comes from an injected clock (countingClock advances one second per call, fixedClock is a frozen instant the test moves forward itself), the staleness window is crossed by moving the injected clock rather than by waiting, and the transaction 'retry' is a deterministic re-invocation of the callback rather than a race. The only durations recorded anywhere are observations, never thresholds.
